grammar_focus: would rather / would sooner 表“宁愿、偏好”(would rather do / would sooner do / would rather ... than ... / would rather + 某人 + 过去式:I'd rather you watched),外加 have sth done“(请人)把某事做好”与 have + 动作名词(have a look)(原创承载 NCE3 L14 考点·净化:把“贵族歹徒勒索保护费”改写为“宁愿凡事亲力亲为的传奇手艺人 Dawson”,保留“被全镇敬重、立牌纪念”的反差,去掉一切犯罪暴力)
scene: 小镇上人人都认识老 Dawson——一个了不起的手艺人。他宁愿自己动手修理一切,也不愿请别人代劳。一场冬天的暴风雨毁掉了他家一段篱笆,邻居们提出替他从城里雇一队工人,他只是笑笑:“我宁愿自己亲手来。”一周之内,整段篱笆又立了起来。镇上大多数人都请公司来修屋顶、修车、翻院子,唯独 Dawson 不肯。他宁愿在漏水的水龙头下待整整一个下午,也不愿打电话叫水管工;宁愿步行五英里,也不愿让人开车送他。每天清早他都爱把工具挨个看一遍,宁愿打着手电干到深夜,也绝不把活儿干一半就撂下。若有小伙子想帮忙,他会和气地说:“我更愿意你在一旁看着学。”谁要不打招呼就拿走他心爱的扳手,他会说:“我希望你别这样。”他做事又快又利落,却分文不取。等他终于老得爬不动梯子,全镇人聚到一起;他去世后,大家在镇政府旁立了一块小铜牌,纪念这位“谁也想不起还有更顽强”的手艺人。乐队奏起乐来,人人都说:宁愿认识一个 Dawson,也胜过认识一百个名人。

grammar_card.title: would rather / would sooner 偏好 + have sth done
grammar_card.intro: ①would rather / would sooner + 动词原形,表示“宁愿做某事”:I would rather stay(我宁愿留下)。②“宁愿做 A 不愿做 B”用 would rather A than B:He would rather walk than wait(他宁愿走也不愿等)。③否定用 would rather not + 原形:I would rather not go。④若“希望别人怎么做”,用 would rather + 某人 + 过去式动词:I'd rather you watched and learned(我更愿意你看着学)/ I'd rather you didn't touch it(我希望你别碰)。⑤have sth done 表示“(请/让别人)把某事做好”:have the roof repaired(请人修屋顶);have + 动作名词表示“做一次”:have a look(看一看)、have a rest(歇一歇)。

specialRules.rule: would rather / would sooner 后面接动词原形(不带 to):I'd rather go(✓)/ I'd rather to go(✗)。
“希望别人”时用 would rather + 某人 + 过去式:I'd rather you came early;否定 I'd rather you didn't。这里的过去式不表示过去,而表示委婉的愿望。
have sth done = 请/让别人做:have your car fixed(让人修车)≠ 自己修;宾位放在 have 和过去分词之间。美语里“水龙头”说 faucet(英式 tap),“手电筒”说 flashlight(英式 torch)。

prelisten.q: Listen and answer — Why wouldn't Old Mr. Dawson let others repair his fence?
options: He would rather do everything himself
He was too busy that week

passage: Everyone in our little town knew Old Mr. Dawson, a remarkable handyman who would rather fix a thing himself than have it done by anyone else. When a winter storm destroyed part of his fence, his neighbors offered to hire a crew from the city, but Dawson only smiled. 'I'd sooner do it with my own two hands,' he said, and he had the whole fence standing again within a week. Most people in town would have their roofs repaired, their cars fixed, and their yards dug by companies. Not Dawson. He would rather spend a whole afternoon under a leaking faucet than call a plumber, and he would sooner walk five miles than have someone drive him. Each morning he liked to have a good look at his tools, and he'd rather work late by flashlight than leave a job half done. If a young man offered to help, Dawson would say kindly, 'I'd rather you watched and learned.' And if anyone picked up his favorite wrench without asking, he'd say, 'I'd rather you didn't.' He fixed everything promptly and never charged a cent. When at last he grew too old to climb ladders, the whole town came together, and after his funeral they dedicated a small brass plaque by the town hall to the memory of the most valiant handyman anyone could remember. A band played, and everyone agreed that they would rather have known one Mr. Dawson than a hundred famous men.
